section_title: What is the church doing when the Holy Spirit calls Barnabas and Saul?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 2 While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

context_lines: Luke names prophets and teachers in the Antioch church: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen and Saul. He notes that Manaen had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch. The list shows several people serving together without specifying that their order establishes a ranking.

While they are worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit directs them to set apart Barnabas and Saul for work to which He has already called them. The initiative comes from the Spirit, and the community responds through fasting, prayer, laying on hands and sending.

The word translated worshiping is **λειτουργέω** (*leitourgeō*, lay-toor-GEH-oh). [Thayer’s entry](https://biblehub.com/greek/3008.htm) describes service rendered to the Lord, including prayer, teaching and other service. Luke names fasting and prayer here but does not give a complete order of worship or identify every activity taking place.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly see the Spirit initiating the mission and the church responding through prayer and a public sending. [Wesley on verse 2](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/) understands this as commissioning people for their appointed work, rather than Saul first becoming an apostle at this moment.
god_plan_lines: This sending moves forward the calling already described in [Acts 9:15–16](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/9.htm). Saul was chosen to carry Jesus’ name before Gentiles, rulers and Israel; the next account will show that witness reaching another place and another hearer.

[Galatians 1:15–16](https://biblehub.com/bsb/galatians/1.htm) describes Paul’s calling by grace to proclaim God’s Son among the Gentiles. Acts places that personal calling within the praying life and practical support of a community. God’s direction and the help of fellow believers are working together in the mission.
current_position_lines: Worship as the Early Church Knew It directly examines the word used in Acts 13:2 as sacred service directed toward the Lord. The study emphasizes active service rather than treating believers as spectators. Here that service is connected with fasting, prayer and responding to the Spirit’s call; Luke does not supply a full list of everything the gathering included.

deeper_study.title: Worship as the Early Church Knew It

editorial_review.position_source_detail: Worship as the Early Church Knew It — Greek Term Leitourgeō; directly develops Acts13:2 as sacred service toward Lord. Limited to active service; no assertion singing certainly absent or all formal worship forbidden.
